slot.brief: Given z satisfying a quadratic-like relation, compute |z| and argument from modulus–conjugate identity 1/z = z̄/|z|².

stem: If $z+\dfrac{1}{z}=\dfrac{3+i}{2}$ and $\operatorname{Im}z>0$, find $\left(|z|,\operatorname{Arg}z\right)$, where $\operatorname{Arg}z$ is principal.

verdicts.working: The roots are obtained from the sum and product: they are 1+i and (1-i)/2. Since only 1+i has positive imaginary part, |z|=√2 and Arg z=π/4.

working:
Write $z=x+iy$, $t=1/|z|^2>0$. Using $1/z=\bar z/|z|^2$: $x(1+t)=\dfrac32$, $y(1-t)=\dfrac12$. Substituting $x=\dfrac{3}{2(1+t)}$, $y=\dfrac{1}{2(1-t)}$ into $x^2+y^2=1/t$ gives $(2t^2-5t+2)(t^2+1)=0$. Since $y>0$, $t=\dfrac12$; hence $z=1+i$, so $|z|=\sqrt2$ and $\operatorname{Arg}z=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

Independent check: The roots are obtained from the sum and product: they are 1+i and (1-i)/2. Since only 1+i has positive imaginary part, |z|=√2 and Arg z=π/4.
solution: From $z+\dfrac1z=\dfrac{3+i}{2}$, we get $z^2-\dfrac{3+i}{2}z+1=0$, whose roots are $1+i$ and $\dfrac{1-i}{2}$. Since $\operatorname{Im}z>0$, $z=1+i$; hence $|z|=\sqrt2$ and $\operatorname{Arg}z=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.
